study2.status_at_freeze: all training complete; sealed efficacy split unopened
study2.purpose: Prospective sealed efficacy evaluation of the already-trained checkpoints under a reward-eligible implementation contract.

disclosure: Study 1 is preserved and remains invalid under its all-distinct-candidate pre-open gate.
Study 1 stopped before rf_training_contract.json and before any eval_sealed.py invocation.
No sealed member, policy candidate, oracle outcome, PPA result, or efficacy endpoint existed or was inspected before this Study 2 freeze.
Study 2 reuses the five already-trained checkpoints without retraining, checkpoint selection, seed addition, or hyperparameter change.
Study 2 is prospective for sealed efficacy but is not an independent validation of the gate population, which was specified after diagnosing the Study 1 failure.

sections: training except the now-complete historical execution record
all endpoint, bootstrap, synthesis, sample-count, seed, checkpoint, decoding, and failure-scoring rules

training_inputs.checkpoint_rule: Use only the already-declared update-138 RF midpoints and update-276 endpoints; no model selection.

reward_eligible_gate.scientific_scope: The implementation contract covers exactly the candidates whose correctness gate allowed the RF structural reward to be evaluated during training.
reward_eligible_gate.eligibility: A row is reward-eligible iff RTL is non-empty, correct is exactly true, gate is exactly 'ok', reward is finite and positive, struct_features is a dictionary, and canon_hash is non-empty.
mandatory_row_checks: Every correct row must be reward-eligible; a missing gate, canonical hash, feature dictionary, or positive finite reward invalidates Study 2.
Every non-correct row must have reward exactly 0.0.
Every source group must contain exactly candidate ids 0 through 7.
A distinct normalized RTL content may not mix eligibility status or design identity.
Every excluded row remains counted by reason and source; no row is deleted from the audit ledger.
eligible_candidate_contract: Materialize every distinct eligible normalized RTL content from both complete RF logs.
Require the lexical canonicalization contract to accept it.
Recompute its canonical hash and structural features and require exact equality to reward-time logged values for every occurrence.
Compile and run original-versus-canonical trace equivalence with both oracle seeds through canonicalize.py trace_equal.
Reject canonical collisions that merge different design identities.
reward_eligible_gate.count_disclosure: These training-log counts were observed during the read-only diagnosis of Study 1's gate failure and are frozen before any sealed efficacy generation. They are validation inputs, not efficacy outcomes.
reward_eligible_gate.failure_rule: Any count mismatch, row error, mixed identity, eligible rejection, exception, reward-time metadata mismatch, compile/trace failure, or cross-design collision invalidates Study 2 and stops before sealed generation. There is no patch-and-rerun within Study 2.

execution_order: Re-verify all five training runs and checkpoints.
Run the reward-eligible audit and write its complete manifest and contract, including exclusions and failures.
Open the sealed split only if the gate passes exactly.
Generate every inherited frozen evaluation arm once.
Run the inherited single laptop Vivado flow over every distinct correct candidate.
Run the inherited fail-closed analysis with the Study 2 contract artifact.
stop_rules: No retraining, resumption, checkpoint selection, new seed, reward change, corpus change, or evaluation change.
No efficacy output may pre-exist the Study 2 server launch.
No sealed candidate or endpoint may be inspected before the complete reward-eligible gate passes.
If the gate fails, preserve it and stop; do not repair and rerun Study 2.
After sealed generation starts, preserve and report the inherited outcome exactly; do not tune or add samples after viewing results.
